description: A desert mountain near Siwa Oasis famous for hot sand-burial therapy, where patients are buried up to the neck in sand heated to around 50C for short sessions during summer.
treated_conditions: Rheumatism, Arthritis, Chronic joint pain, Muscle pain
mineral_composition: Fine desert sand, no water mineral content (dry heat therapy)
best_visit_season: Summer (Jun-Aug) for sand therapy; Oct-Apr for general visit
nearby_attractions: Siwa Fortress (Shali), Temple of the Oracle, Cleopatra Spring
facilities_available: Basic; some eco-lodges nearby (e.g., Adrere Amellal)
historical_use: Traditional Siwan/Bedouin remedy used for generations
safety_notes: Sand can reach very high temperatures in peak summer; hydration essential

description: Natural sulfur/mineral springs and salt lakes around Siwa town, used for bathing, muscle relaxation and skin conditions.
treated_conditions: Skin conditions, Muscle relaxation, General wellness
nearby_attractions: Gebel El-Dakrur, Siwa Fortress, Temple of the Oracle
facilities_available: Basic pools, some developed for tourists
historical_use: Named after Cleopatra; used historically by locals for bathing
safety_notes: Some springs unregulated; check water clarity before bathing

place_name_ar: بئر الغبة وعين العيون - الواحات البحرية
place_name_en: Bir Al-Ghaba & Eyebath Spring - Bahariya Oasis
description: Hot springs in Bahariya Oasis; Bir Al-Ghaba is used for relaxing baths while the sulfur-rich 'Eyebath' spring is traditionally used for eye ailments.
nearby_attractions: Black Desert, White Desert National Park, Valley of the Golden Mummies
facilities_available: Basic; camps and lodges in Bawiti town

description: A self-flowing sulfurous hot spring developed into an open-air jacuzzi-style pool in the desert near Farafra.
nearby_attractions: White Desert National Park, Crystal Mountain
historical_use: Long-used informal bathing site for locals and desert travelers
safety_notes: No supervision; remote location, arrange transport in advance

description: Sulfur and mineral springs scattered around Kharga Oasis, traditionally used for rheumatic and skin conditions.

A Red Sea resort town globally known for its black, sulfur-rich sand and saline sea water, considered one of the best places worldwide for treating psoriasis and arthritis, aided by the dry, pollen-free air.
mineral_composition: Sulfur-rich black sand, high-salinity sea water
nearby_attractions: Hurghada resorts, Red Sea diving/snorkeling sites
facilities_available: Developed resorts and dedicated psoriasis/arthritis clinics
historical_use: Established medical tourism hub since the 20th century
safety_notes: Follow clinic guidance on sun/sand exposure duration
price_description: Free beach access; clinic treatment packages priced separately

description: A Red Sea coastal town close to Cairo, known for hot mineral springs used to treat arthritis and joint/muscle pain, combined with a relaxed beach resort setting.
nearby_attractions: Galala Mountain, Red Sea beach resorts
historical_use: Popular weekend retreat and therapeutic destination for Cairenes

description: Hot sulfur springs flowing from Mount Hammam Pharaoun on the Gulf of Suez, used for centuries to treat arthritis, skin disease and respiratory ailments.
nearest_airport: Sharm El-Sheikh International Airport (SSH) or Cairo (CAI)
nearby_attractions: Ras Sedr beaches, Gulf of Suez coast
facilities_available: Basic; boat access required to reach spring source
historical_use: Used since Pharaonic times per local tradition; long-standing folk remedy
safety_notes: Water very hot at source; access only with local guide/boat

description: One of Egypt's oldest sulfur springs, located near the Sinai entrance, traditionally used for rheumatic conditions and skin ailments.
nearby_attractions: Suez Canal area, Sinai desert landscapes
historical_use: Associated with biblical tradition; long folk-medicine use
safety_notes: Unregulated site; check current condition before visiting

description: A district south of Cairo with natural sulfur springs and the Helwan Medical Center for Sulfur, Rheumatism and Natural Medicine, established in 1955, offering specialized rheumatism treatment.
nearby_attractions: Wadi Degla Protectorate, Japanese Garden Helwan
facilities_available: Established medical center with formal treatment programs

description: Mineral-rich springs in the Fayoum area used traditionally for skin and joint conditions, set within a garden/park setting.
nearby_attractions: Wadi El Rayan, Lake Qarun, Tunis Village

description: Aswan's dry, warm desert climate (not a spring) is recommended for respiratory and rheumatic patients, as low humidity reduces inflammation triggers; often combined with Nile-side relaxation and nearby ancient sites.
nearby_attractions: Philae Temple, Aswan High Dam, Nubian Villages
safety_notes: Stay hydrated; very hot in summer months
medical_supervision_details: No dedicated clinic; general hospitals available in city

description: Natural sulfur and mineral hot springs scattered around Dakhla Oasis (near Mut town), similar in character to the springs of neighboring Kharga Oasis, traditionally used by locals for rheumatism and skin conditions.
nearby_attractions: Al-Qasr Old Town, Deir el-Hagar Temple, Balat village
historical_use: Traditional local bathing site, long-standing folk remedy
safety_notes: Unregulated site; verify current condition and access before visiting

description: Man-made caves built from rock salt extracted from Siwa's salt lakes, used for halotherapy (salt-air inhalation therapy). Marsa Matrouh has more than one such cave (e.g., the Bedouin Village cave on Salloum Road and Salman's Salt Cave on the western Corniche).
treated_conditions: Respiratory diseases, Allergies, Thyroid-related stress, Psychological stress/relaxation
mineral_composition: Rock salt (halite) from Siwa salt lakes
nearby_attractions: Cleopatra Beach, Rommel's Cave Museum, Agiba Beach
facilities_available: Purpose-built salt caves with seating, part of tourist village setups
historical_use: Modern concept (developed over the last ~15 years), inspired by Siwa's salt resources

description: A palm-shaded oasis in Tor Sinai city with 5 sulfur springs reaching about 37C, distinct from Ayun Musa in Ras Sedr. Studies note the springs' ability to treat skin diseases and rheumatism; the site spans about 628,000 sqm with over 2,000 fruiting palm trees, a domed bathhouse, swimming pools, and a beach area.
nearest_airport: Sharm El-Sheikh International Airport (SSH) or St. Catherine Airport
nearby_attractions: El-Kilani Greek Orthodox Church/ruins, Tor Sinai coastline, Saint Catherine Monastery (further inland)
facilities_available: Domed sulfur bathhouse, swimming pools, palm oasis, beach area; eco-hotel and therapy center reported under development
historical_use: Long-standing local/religious tradition (named after Prophet Moses); recently reopened for organized tourism
safety_notes: Separate bathing hours for men and women in the domed spring bath
medical_supervision_details: No (recreational bathhouse; a dedicated therapeutic activity center has been built but was not yet operational as of the latest reports)
